The train station says “the person at the botanical garden tells the truth,” so the train station is false. The gym says “the person at the train station lies,” so the gym is true. The shopping mall says “the person at the gym tells the truth,” so the shopping mall is true. The skate park says “the person at the shopping mall lies,” so the skate park is false. The campground says “the person at the skate park lies,” so the campground is true. Thus campground yes, skate park no, shopping mall yes; my response gives exactly “**yes, no, yes**.”

It ignores the explicit “The person at the planetarium lies” when reaching its conclusion.
